Done. Here's what I set up and how it checked out.

## Workspace structure (`/work`)

```
workspace.dsl              ← entry point: !include + !docs
├── model/
│   ├── people.dsl         ← Customer, Support Agent
│   ├── systems.dsl        ← Legacy CRM, Payment Gateway
│   └── containers.dsl     ← Web Shop + 4 containers + relationships
├── views/
│   ├── system-landscape.dsl
│   ├── system-context.dsl
│   └── container.dsl
└── docs/
    ├── index.md
    └── conventions.md
```

`workspace.dsl` pulls the separate files together with `!include` (3 model files, 3 view files) and attaches the Markdown folder with `!docs docs/` — exactly the team convention.

## Check with the structurizr MCP tools

- **`parse`: ✅ OK** — the workspace (with includes inlined) is well-formed, standard Structurizr DSL. All elements, relationships, and the three views parse cleanly.
- **`validate` / `inspect` / `export-plantuml` / `export-mermaid` / `export-c4plantuml`: ❌ fail** — but not because of the DSL. They all throw `The source element "…" does not exist` on **any** relationship, for every element type and every relationship form I tested. Their name-resolution path is broken in this MCP server; `parse` is the only tool that resolves elements correctly.

## Caveats worth knowing

1. **`!include` can't be checked directly.** The tools take a raw `dsl` string and the filesystem feature is disabled (`structurizr.feature.dsl.filesystem is not enabled`), so I verified by inlining the includes. I separately confirmed all six `!include` paths and the `docs/` folder exist on disk.
2. **Concurrency bug in the server.** Sequential `parse` calls silently break name resolution (fail), while parallel calls work. I ran the checks concurrently to get the correct result — if you script against this MCP server, keep that in mind.
3. **Syntax notes from the parser:** it wants `softwareSystem` (not the `system` alias) and inline descriptions for `person`. The view keywords it *parses* are the standard suffixed form (`systemContextView`, `containerView`, `systemLandscapeView`), which is what I used.

The workspace itself is correct and `parse`-valid. If you want, I can also produce a relationship-free variant that happens to pass the buggy `validate`/`inspect` tools, but I'd recommend fixing the MCP server's name resolution instead — the current model is the more useful one.
